children: Glass Wall Systems (India) shares made a modest debut on the stock market but gained momentum after listing, trading with over 13 per cent gains from the offer price of ₹182. The stock listed at a 6.5 per cent premium at ₹194 on the NSE and later climbed on the BSE.
On the BSE, Glass Wall Systems shares listed at a 4.4 per cent premium at ₹190.10 and subsequently soared to a high of ₹206.85.

Shivani Nyati, Head of Wealth at Swastika Investmart, said the brokerage’s subscribe view remains supported by 64 per cent FY26 revenue growth, ₹83.8 crore PAT, 43 per cent ROCE, 38.6 per cent ROE and a ₹846-crore order book. Investors should monitor execution, real-estate demand and overseas exposure, she added, with a stop loss of ₹178.
The company’s ₹428-crore initial share sale was subscribed 81.65 times. The IPO received bids for 1,34,37,27,276 shares against 1,64,57,298 shares on offer.
The QIB portion was subscribed 167.93 times, while the non-institutional investor category received 79.71 times subscription. The retail investors quota was subscribed 33.18 times.
Glass Wall Systems had fixed a price band of ₹172-182 per share for its IPO.

The mainboard issue comprised a fresh issuance of equity shares worth up to ₹60 crore and an offer-for-sale of 2.02 crore equity shares by promoters Jawahar Hariram Hemrajani and Eshan Jawahar Hemrajani, and investor shareholder India Business Excellence Fund IIA.

Of the proceeds from the fresh issue, ₹50 crore will be utilised for setting up a glass processing unit as part of the company’s planned backward integration at its Vile Bhagad facility in Maharashtra.
The remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes.

title: Glass Wall Systems stock lists at 6.5% premium on NSE
